name: Ipswich
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Ipswich, MA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Ipswich, MA: the Jingle Bell Walk, Castle Hill's Artful Christmas, Santa at Littles Lounge and Marini Farm crafts.
lede: Ipswich has a high school run Jingle Bell Walk to Santa's Village, a decorated Great House at Castle Hill, Santa visits at a play cafe and farm crafts.
celebrates: Ipswich keeps Christmas close to the water and downtown. The Jingle Bell Walk, presented by Ipswich High School Interact and supported by the Ipswich-Rowley Rotary Club, starts at Town Wharf, follows Water Street along the river and ends in Santa's Village in Town Hall. The Greater Cape Ann Chamber of Commerce lists a Downtown Holiday Stroll with local merchants the same day. The Trustees decorate the Great House at Castle Hill for An Artful Christmas, while Marini Farm and Littles Lounge Play Cafe run kid sized holiday crafts and Santa sessions.
lastyear: The Local News listed the Jingle Bell Walk in its weekly roundup published on December 10, 2025, with Mr. Kringle arriving at Town Wharf at 11 am before leading a procession. That roundup also mentioned a downtown holiday stroll. The pattern has stayed the same this year, with Santa meeting families at the wharf and a walk to Town Hall for crafts and games.
facts: Castle Hill on the Crane Estate is cared for by the Trustees, and its Great House is the centerpiece of An Artful Christmas, with rooms inspired by masterworks from artists including Monet, Van Gogh, Botticelli and Kahlo. The Jingle Bell Walk is run by teens in the Interact service club, and the Rotary says it is a community institution that returns each year. Families are asked to bring an unwrapped toy for a regional holiday toy drive.
trains: Ipswich has its own MBTA Commuter Rail station on the Newburyport/Rockport Line, with trains from North Station through Salem, Beverly and Hamilton/Wenham. The next stops north are Rowley and Newburyport, and the line continues to Gloucester and Rockport on the other branch. For a holiday train ride, Edaville in Carver runs trains through Christmas lights, and the Boston Street Railway Association shows historic streetcars.

faq: What is the Ipswich Jingle Bell Walk?

It is a holiday walk presented by Ipswich High School Interact. It begins at Town Wharf, continues along Water Street beside the river and ends in Santa's Village in Town Hall. The Ipswich-Rowley Rotary Club asks families to bring an unwrapped toy for the North Shore and Merrimack Valley Holiday Toy Drive.
Where can kids meet Santa in Ipswich?

Kids can meet Santa at the Town Wharf at the start of the Jingle Bell Walk, then in Santa's Village at Town Hall. Littles Lounge Play Cafe on High Street also holds ticketed Santa sessions with storytime, photos and open play, so check its online calendar for dates.
Is Castle Hill good for kids at Christmas?

The Trustees say kids can try a Crane holiday eye spy and that cookies and hot chocolate are mentioned for visitors. They also offer sensory friendly hours with reduced capacity, no music and no flickering lights. The Grand Stair has 30 steps and there is no elevator, which matters for strollers.
What can families do at Marini Farm at Christmas?

Marini Farm runs Kid's Christmas Cookie Decorating, where kids frost and decorate holiday themed cookies, and Parent and Child Wreath Decorating in a heated greenhouse. Space is limited and tickets are sold online, so book ahead through the farm's event pages.
Can I take a train to Ipswich?

Yes. Ipswich has a station on the MBTA Newburyport/Rockport Line, with service from North Station through Salem and Beverly. The station is a stop between Hamilton/Wenham and Rowley. Edaville in Carver is a longer trip for a holiday train ride through Christmas lights.
